answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring each agent to lock collateral before it may trade. Randomly selected trusted peers audit its claims on tasks such as karst mapping, comet tracking, or plume forecasting; good results earn fees and reputation, while duplicate identities or coordinated false reports trigger slashing. A Sybil attacker must fund each fake account and risk losing each deposit, so multiplying identities makes the attacker's expected loss grow linearly.
